newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK govt says total exports up two pct in Q1 1997.
newsitem.headline: HK govt says total exports up two pct in Q1 1997.

text.p: The Hong Kong government said on Friday total exports rose by two percent in value terms to HK$314 billion in the first quarter of 1997 over a year earlier. "As there was a modest decline in export prices, the increase in real terms was about four percent, only slightly below the five percent growth in the fourth quarter of 1996," the government said in its First Quarter Economic Report 1997.
Within this total, re-exports rose by four percent in value terms over a year earlier to HK$269.0 billion in the first quarter of 1997.
After discounting price changes, the growth rate in real terms was about five percent. This followed an eight percent increase in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Domestic exports fell by six percent in value terms over a year earlier to HK$45 billion in the first quarter of 1997.
"The decrease in real terms was about four percent, much less significant than the decline of 10 percent and seven percent in the preceding two quarters," the government said.

The value of imports rose by four percent over a year earlier to HK$362 billion in the first quarter of 1997. After netting out price changes, the increase in real terms was about six percent, the same as in the fourth quarter of 1996.
The government reported a visible trade deficit of HK$48.2 billion, equivalent to 13.3 percent of the value of imports in the first quarter of 1997.
Corresponding figures in the first quarter of 1996 were HK$39.8 billion and 11.5 percent.
